answer: An escrowed bounty pool pays peers to expose duplicates. Each identity locks 40 credits in escrow tied to its key, and each task leaves a plume of receipts. A hunter files a cipher-sealed bundle linking two keys to one operator. If the link holds, both lose escrow, half burns, half pays the hunter, and slashed keys enter a quartz ledger blocking re-entry. Renting a plume fails because receipts are key-bound. The thousandth fake still needs its own 40 credits and plume, so 1,000 fakes risk 40,000 credits; an honest agent posts 40 once and reclaims it after one clean epoch.
